PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT / WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM (Nov. 8, 2024) - Kevin Brashear to Monica Tran-Nguyen
Re: Unified Litigation Hold - Custodians, Data Sources, Spoliation Exposure, Coordination (Kovach / SEC)

1. BOTTOM LINE
- Issue one consolidated hold today, tagged by matter (K = Kovach; S = SEC). Do not wait for Monday: Teams chats and Salesforce records are being deleted nightly, and no hold of any kind exists on any system (Novotny memo Sec. 2.2, 3.2).
- Trigger: our own Retention Policy Sec. 4.1(f) and (h) list "whistleblower complaints" and "commencement of an internal investigation" as triggers. That makes Aug. 5, 2024 (Kovach letter) the defensible trigger and Aug. 20 (Pinnacle investigation) the outer bound; Stadler Raines asserts Aug. 5; Sept. 12 is too late. Oct. 3 (demand with preservation demand), Oct. 28 (SEC notice; Policy 4.1(g)) are indisputable. Assume Aug. 5 for exposure planning.
- Real loss has occurred: Teams chats created roughly May 7-Aug. 8, 2024 are gone, covering every Kovach complaint (June 14, 28; July 2), the July 2-15 window Stadler Raines singled out, and the PIP. Some loss occurred even after the Oct. 3 demand. Email is largely intact; Salesforce, NXF-FS01 and the iPhone are the next losses.
- Exposure is serious but not necessarily sanctionable: loss stems from a pre-dispute routine policy, but continued purging after Oct. 3/Oct. 28 is hard to defend.

2. ACTIONS TODAY (authorize in writing; Policy 4.2 step 4 requires IT written confirmation)
1) Suspend Teams 90-day chat purge tenant-wide (not custodian-only). Also suspend the 1-year channel purge before Jan. 2025, when Q1 2024 channel posts begin to expire.
2) Suspend Salesforce 2:00 a.m. inactive-record batch job; check 15-day recycle bin; Data Loader export of channel account/opportunity records (1-2 days).
3) M365 eDiscovery holds (mailbox, OneDrive, Teams) for all Tier 1-3 custodians plus Kovach's converted shared mailbox and OneDrive.
4) Forensic image of NXF-FS01 (8-10 hours) now, before further SharePoint migration; halt "stale" file deletion. Place Veritas Vault (NXF-EV01) on hold; image it.
5) Locate Kovach's returned Dell laptop (personnel file: returned Sept. 12; absent from IT inventory). Quarantine and image; confirm not reimaged.
6) Cross-reference Vault remediation log (421 mailboxes) against custodian list; expedite remediation only under forensic documentation.
7) Export M365 unified audit logs now (retention period unverified; ask Ridgeway) - the only surviving metadata for purged chats.
8) Freeze residual backups (Policy 3.6: rolling 90 days); ask whether any Exchange backups survived the May 15, 2024 decommissioning.
9) Collections by IT/Ridgeway under chain-of-custody protocol, never self-collection by custodians involved in the allegations.

3. TRIGGER TIMELINE AND LOSS ASSESSMENT (90-day Teams chat window; chats on hand at each date)
Aug. 5 trigger: chats back to May 7 would have survived. Aug. 20: May 22. Aug. 29 (Kovach tells Pinnacle he used Teams): June 1. Sept. 12: June 14, exactly his first complaint. Oct. 3: July 5. Oct. 28: July 30. Nov. 6: Aug. 8 (my earlier calculation confirmed). Each day deletes another day.
Assessment by source:
- Teams chats: LOST for about May 7-Aug. 8 (post-Aug. 5 trigger); chats created July 5-Aug. 8 were lost after the Oct. 3 demand specifically demanding Teams preservation. Unrecoverable per IT (ask Ridgeway to test Substrate recovery). Pre-May 7 chats (Q1 quarter-end) were lost before any trigger, but the SEC period begins Jan. 1.
- Salesforce: records marked inactive before about May 8, 2023 are already deleted (18 months). Deletions after Aug. 5 cover records marked inactive Feb. 5-May 8, 2023; after Oct. 3, Apr. 3-May 8, 2023. Roughly 2,200 FY2023 inactive records; subset unknown. Quantify before any representation to SEC/Stadler Raines.
- Email: M365 retains 7 years; Kovach mailbox intact post-April 1, 2024 (converted to shared mailbox, no hold). Vault: nothing purged. Gap: 421 mailboxes (~15%) incompletely ingested; Exchange volumes deallocated May 15, 2024 (pre-trigger, so likely not spoliation, but a Q1 2024 collection gap SEC will see). Kovach forwarding to Herrera ran Sept. 12-Oct. 12.
- NXF-FS01 and SAP: no loss yet. SAP no deletion risk; preserve change logs/document timestamps (Jessup: "ship-ahead" shipments preceded SAP order finalization).
- iPhone: unmanaged; any loss unknown.
- Paper: HR file and Sales 8th-floor files (contents unconfirmed): freeze and inventory.

4. CUSTODIANS (K = Kovach, S = SEC; both = unified)
Tier 1 (hold today, forensic collection)
- Kovach (data in company control: mailbox, OneDrive, laptop, Teams, Salesforce, S:\ activity) - both.
- Renata Sokolova, CFO: June 14/July 2 complaints; "make the number"; PIP weekly reports to CFO; rev-rec - both.
- Graham Ellicott, CEO: approved PIP, terminated, FY reviews; "senior leadership" directive suspected (Herrera) - both.
- Janet Purdy, VP HR: PIP, check-in notes, termination, HRIS (SuccessFactors) - K primarily; S marginal.
- Li Wei Chen, Controller: June 28 complaint, ASC 606 entries, return reserves - both.
- Tomas Herrera: Salesforce "inactive" designations, sales directives; interim VP (conflict: remove his control over relevant data) - both.
- Marcus Ainsley, Audit Committee Chair (Sec. 8) - both.
Tier 2 (S-primary; K-relevant as pretext/comparator evidence)
- Brett Collings, Diana Munoz, Raj Patwardhan (RSMs; texts to distributors, informal return assurances, directive emails), Frank Jessup (VP Operations; Houston/Dallas distribution), 11 other regional managers (targeted hold), three Sales Ops staff.
- Controller/revenue-accounting staff, FP&A, Investor Relations, Internal Audit, Corporate Secretary (board materials, SEC request 6), Sokolova's and Ellicott's executive assistants, other Audit Committee members' committee communications.
Tier 3 (systems/process): Novotny, Halverson, Dasgupta, Salesforce admins, SAP Basis, IT Service Desk, logistics staff. Their records show who decided the 90-day policy.
Third parties: Caldwell Thornton (auditor; SEC request 7); Pinnacle investigation file (Cross notes, Patwardhan emails).
Unique to one matter: K-only: Purdy's HR staff, IT Service Desk. S-only: Jessup, logistics, accounting/IR/Internal Audit staff, Corporate Secretary, auditor. Both: Tier 1 and RSMs.
Relevant period: recommend Jan. 1, 2023-present for sales/finance (prior-year comparatives drove Cross's analysis; 3.1% historical return baseline); personnel/reviews from hire (FY2021-23 ratings are pretext evidence); SEC period Jan. 1-Sept. 30, 2024 minimum; continuing.

5. INTERVIEWEES (Monica's question)
All seven current interviewees (Sokolova, Chen, Herrera, Collings, Munoz, Patwardhan, Jessup) are custodians (above); the eighth, Kovach, is a former-employee custodian. Collings, Munoz, Patwardhan and Jessup had no termination role but are SEC-critical.

6. DATA SOURCES
M365 mail/calendar/OneDrive/SharePoint; Teams chat (purge suspended), channels, files; Veritas Vault; Salesforce (US org; job suspended); SAP S/4HANA (snapshot; change logs); NXF-FS01 (image); SuccessFactors HRIS; M365 audit logs; corporate Dell laptop; paper HR and Sales files; text messages and personal phones (BYOD covers only about 45 VP+; RSMs who texted distributors are outside the program and unmanaged, so issue individual device instructions); voicemail; corporate credit card records; board portal materials. Monterrey: Kovach's territories are described as US-only (personnel file; Cross) but "US, Canada, Mexico, Central and South America" in the demand letter. Resolve; meanwhile preserve NXF-MTY-FS01 and the Monterrey Salesforce org (low cost).

7. KOVACH iPHONE AND PRESERVATION DEMAND
- No technical access exists, but Kovach signed a BYOD acknowledgment (Jan. 8, 2021) agreeing to "cooperate with data preservation and collection requirements as directed by the Legal Department" and to inspection of work data. Cite it in Drummond's letter. It cuts both ways: it may support a "control" argument, and no request was made at termination.
- Letter (through Stadler Raines only; Kovach is represented) should demand preservation of Outlook, Teams (cached chats), Salesforce app data, texts, iCloud backups; propose neutral-vendor imaging. Expect reciprocal scrutiny of our gap; send anyway.

8. AINSLEY PROTOCOL
- Preserve first; privilege review follows. Privilege is not a ground to defer or narrow the hold. Hold any Nexfield mailbox/board portal; ask Ainsley in writing about personal email, phones and texts.
- Concur with two-track review (Track 1: Aug. 5 letter, factual responses; Track 2: Audit Committee deliberations with counsel, logged). Caution on having Pinnacle collect: it ran the investigation (Cross memo), is now defense counsel (Oct. 18 letter), and is a likely fact witness on the investigation and on termination timing. Recommend Ridgeway collect under an independent privilege-screen attorney, with Pinnacle directing only.
- Privilege holders differ: Audit Committee (investigation, Aug. 20-Oct. 10) versus Company (defense engagement); Pinnacle's letter says do not commingle. Confirm who controls waiver of the Cross memo (addressed to you and Ainsley) before using it.
- Garner v. Wolfinbarger, 430 F.2d 1093 (5th Cir. 1970) (shareholder good-cause exception), adopted in Delaware in Wal-Mart Stores v. Indiana Elec. Workers Pension Trust Fund, 95 A.3d 1264 (Del. 2014); not verified in this review. Risk is derivative-suit-specific (Kovach is not a shareholder); log Track 2 rigorously.

9. SPOLIATION LAW AND RISK
- Federal: Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e) (ESI lost after duty arose, no reasonable steps, not restorable): prejudice permits curative measures; only intent to deprive permits adverse inference or dismissal. Fifth Circuit: adverse inference requires bad faith; negligence insufficient. Guzman v. Jones, 804 F.3d 707, 713 (5th Cir. 2015) (verified by search snippet only). Duty arises when party knows or should know evidence may be relevant (same). Texas state-court analogue: Brookshire Bros. v. Aldridge, 438 S.W.3d 9 (Tex. 2014) (not re-verified).
- Application: no suit is pending; OSHA complaint deadline is 180 days from Sept. 12 (about Mar. 11, 2025) per demand letter and 29 C.F.R. 1980.103(d) (not re-verified). Rule 37(e) bites once in federal court; the more immediate risk is 18 U.S.C. 1519 (destruction "in relation to or contemplation of" a federal matter; no pending proceeding required; cited in our own Policy Sec. 1, 4.3) plus SEC credibility. Intent facts against us: Policy 4.1 triggers; the 90-day setting conflicts with Policy 3.6 (align cloud settings to retention schedules); purging continued after written demands. Facts for us: policy tenant-wide and pre-dispute; Vault and email intact; replacement sources (email, SAP, Salesforce, Kovach's device, interviews, audit-log metadata) may substitute for lost chats.
- Candor: prepare an accurate preservation narrative for Stadler Raines and SEC; never imply a hold existed earlier.

10. COORDINATION
- Unified hold: one notice with matter annexes; 48-hour acknowledgments, hold log, quarterly reminders (Policy 4.2-4.3); only GC/AGC may release; add non-retaliation reminder.
- Pinnacle: the Oct. 18 engagement covers only Kovach claims, and our copy is unsigned. No counsel is engaged for the SEC inquiry (response due Nov. 27). Resolve now. The Nov. 2 Stadler Raines response date has passed: confirm whether we responded.
- Ridgeway (engaged Nov. 1): holds, imaging, audit-log export, within Legal-directed scope.
- IT: NXF-FS01 decommissioning (Jan. 31, 2025); Policy 3.6 requires 60 days' written notice to Legal (due Dec. 2) and Legal's written release before destruction. Confirm whether given.
- Auditor: preservation request to Caldwell Thornton via Audit Committee.
- Per your instruction, findings go to Drummond only in this memo, but Section 2 IT directions should issue today regardless.

11. DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCIES AND OPEN ITEMS
- Kovach BYOD enrollment: IT says Apr. 3, 2020 (Outlook provisioning); HR says about Jan. 2021 (acknowledgment Jan. 8, 2021); BYOD policy covers VP and above and Kovach became VP Jan. 1, 2021. HR lists Salesforce mobile app; IT lists only Outlook/Teams.
- Hire title: Regional Sales Manager (HR, Cross) vs Director (demand).
- Reporting line: personnel file says Kovach reported to Ellicott with dotted line to Sokolova; demand letter calls Sokolova his supervisor.
- Your titles: "Deputy General Counsel" (emails) vs "General Counsel" (all other documents). Policy (rev. Feb. 2023, approved by you as GC) refers to the Microsoft 365 migration that occurred Apr. 2024, and IT says the Teams policy was set in Feb. 2023 with the "prior General Counsel's office": reconcile policy revision history and who approved the 90-day setting.
- Policy 3.3 requires 7-year retention of distributor agreements, yet Salesforce deletes inactive accounts at 18 months and FS01 "stale" files will be deleted: existing policy violations independent of the hold.
- Unresolved: whether Kovach/Sokolova/Chen mailboxes are among the 421; actual Salesforce deletion volume; Substrate recoverability; laptop status; whether any Teams data lived on other devices; Monterrey scope; who approved the Teams 90-day policy.
